status.summary: Show the branch, what is staged, what changed and what git does not track yet.

examples.1: The short version

examples.1: Stop tracking a file, keep it on your disk

examples.1: Stage tracked files and commit in one go
examples.2: Replace the last commit (only before you push it)

examples.1: Include origin/* branches

examples.1: Fetch and rebase your work on top

All branches as a graph

about.title: Practice the skills you use every day
about.intro: Grindstone is a training ground for developers: short, game-like levels that run in your browser. The first track is git, because everyone uses it and almost everyone is a little afraid of rebase.

teammates.title: You are not alone in the repo
teammates.text: Simulated teammates push to origin while you work. Keeping your branch in sync, rebasing onto a moved main and force-pushing safely only make sense when others change things too.

real.title: It feels like the real thing
real.text: Commands and messages follow real git, down to "rejected, fetch first". What you practise here carries over to your own terminal.

graph.title: You see what git does
graph.text: Every command redraws a live commit graph, so branches, merges and rebases stop being invisible.

ide.title: Work the way you work
ide.text: Use a plain terminal, or an IDE layout with files, an editor with conflict actions and a terminal below.

about.how: Everything runs in your browser: Grindstone has its own git simulation in TypeScript, so levels are predictable, undo is instant and nothing is sent anywhere. Your progress stays on your device. The code is open source.

later.tracks: More tracks: working with AI, web fundamentals, debugging, framework deep dives
later.profile: A skill profile that shows where you are strong and what to practise next

about.by: Grindstone is built by Dominik Kiessling, a frontend and full-stack developer working with Vue, Nuxt and TypeScript.

done.title: Every {track} level solved
done.text: You solved all {n} levels. New chapters are on the way; until then, replay any level or keep the cheat sheet close.

entry.title: Mark “{name}” as not solved?
entry.text: “{name}” goes back to not solved: its best run, latest run, “practise again” flag and where you left off are cleared. This cannot be undone.

chapter.title: Reset chapter {chapter}?
chapter.text: {solved}, their best runs, “practise again” flags and where you left off in {chapter} are cleared. This cannot be undone.

track.title: Reset all {track} progress?
track.text: {solved}, their best runs, “practise again” flags and where you left off in the {track} track are cleared. This cannot be undone.

all.title: Reset everything?
all.text: All progress in this browser is cleared: {solved}, their best runs, “practise again” flags and where you left off. This cannot be undone.

backup.title: Your progress
backup.intro: Stored only in this browser. Download it to keep a backup or to move to another browser, and load it back there.

error.json: {file} is not a progress file (it is not valid JSON). Nothing was changed.
error.shape: {file} is not a Grindstone progress file. Nothing was changed.
error.version: {file} comes from a newer or unknown version of Grindstone. Nothing was changed.
error.read: Could not read {file}. Nothing was changed.
error.size: {file} is too big to be a progress file (over {max}). Nothing was changed.
error.save: Loaded {file}, but this browser would not store it (storage is blocked or full). It is gone when you close this page; download it again to keep a copy.

replace.title: Replace your progress?
replace.text: Loading {file} ({what}) replaces the progress in this browser ({current}). This cannot be undone; download your current progress first if you want to keep it.
